messages:
morgan: Quick follow-up after the FlashAttention RFC — a few integration/contract questions before we start the canary. TLDR: we saw a ~6-10% p99 latency uplift on mid-seq workloads when enabling v3 kernels; want to confirm expected surface area for fallbacks and how to expose toggle points.

alex: Thanks. Can you paste the perf snapshot and the exact config you used? v3 has some shape/align preconditions that change workspace usage.

morgan: Pasted below. This was on a 2xA100 node with default per-model config. workload: chat-like mix (max_seq 2048, median 384). batch size 8 typical.
```
perf: p50 32ms -> 31ms, p95 120ms -> 126ms, p99 260ms -> 285ms (v2 -> v3)
alloc: workspace peak +8% on average, fragmentation up ~12% in allocator logs
kernels: flashattn_v2 used for short/packed, flashattn_v3 selected for mid/long sequences by selector
```

morgan: The selector is our new kernel_picker which picks based on seq_len distribution + workspace_avail. It currently prefers v3 for seq>128 if workspace fraction >= 0.6.

tara: Two quick questions: 1) do we have telemetry that records the reason a kernel was chosen (policy, OOM-fallback, shape-incompat)? 2) what's the intended contract between runtime and kernels for 'safe failure' — i.e., how should v3 signal an incompatible workspace vs throwing OOM at the allocator?

samir: On telemetry: we emit kernel_choice,event with tags {kernel, reason, seq_len_bucket, workspace_frac}. But 'reason' is currently just 'policy' or 'fallback' — not granular. We should add 'incompatibility' and 'alloc_error' buckets.

alex: Contract: kernels should return a short error enum, not raise. e.g., the kernel API returns {status: OK|INCOMPATIBLE_SHAPE|INSUFFICIENT_WORKSPACE|RUNTIME_ERROR}. Runtime then either tries fallback kernel or does dynamic workspace resize.

morgan: Good. Wanted to confirm that approach. If kernel returns INSUFFICIENT_WORKSPACE we should attempt: 1) compact allocator (cheap), 2) try v2 kernel (if compatible), 3) if still fail, enqueue with smaller batch. Agree?

tara: Agree, but add a fast-path for 'spill-to-cpu' only for low-throughput critical requests (admin toggle). Not for normal PLG traffic.

samir: Question: dynamic workspace resize is expensive in hot path. Can we use preflight_alloc for v3 to check requirement before launching? Kernel can expose a function: required_workspace(shape, dtype, seq_len) -> bytes. Then runtime does a try_reserve. If reserve fails we skip kernel. That avoids runtime OOM.

alex: Yes, expose required_workspace API. But caveat: v3 may have internal heuristics (cuBLAS workspace) that vary with batch/seq alignment; required_workspace should return upper bound or a safe estimate. We should version that API.

morgan: Noted. Also observed perf regression only at p95/p99 in mid-seq. Hypothesis: v3 does more kernel-invocation overhead for certain packing patterns and loses batching efficiency. We should add microtraces: kernel_invocations_per_request and avg_kv_cache_hits.

samir: I'll add microtraces. Also suggest an A/B: route 10% traffic by seq_bucket to v3 vs v2 with same workspace budget and measure tokens/sec and tail latency. We need about 100k requests to get stable p99.

tara: Rollout checklist idea: (1) add detailed telemetry and new kernel_status enum; (2) implement required_workspace API on v3; (3) add runtime fallback flow for the 3 error enums; (4) run staged AB by seq_bucket; (5) enable canary in Dedicated with higher workspace_frac to validate throughput.

alex: One more: kernel selection policy should be tunable per-customer (dedicated customers may prefer throughput over p99). Let's expose `kernel_preference: [throughput|latency|cost]` and map to selector thresholds.

morgan: Agreed. Any blockers?

alex: Need PR from runtime with the enum + selector change. Also need v3 patch to export required_workspace and return INSUFFICIENT_WORKSPACE instead of crashing.

samir: I'll schedule the telemetry + selector changes today. Can we do a short spike to reproduce the p99 bump on a repro harness (send me the exact prompt mix)?

morgan: Sending sample harness in DM. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: runtime/kernels/selectors v1.3 -> canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC (notify #eng-oncall on deploy)

tara: Leaving note — keep an eye on allocator fragmentation metric 'gpu_alloc_frag' during canary. If it rises >15% abort and revert.

morgan: Will do. We'll reconvene after canary results.
